subject: general
question: In an electric generator, __________ energy is used to rotate a conductor in a _________ field to produce electricity.
solution:
The correct answer is __**mechanical, magnetic**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is used to rotate the conductor in an electric generator.
 
• The rotation occurs within a **magnetic field** to produce electricity.
 
• This process is fundamental to the working of many power generation systems, including those in power plants.
 
• The conversion of mechanical energy to electrical energy is a key principle in electromagnetic induction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday** is credited with the discovery of electromagnetic induction, which is the working principle behind electric generators.
 
• Electric generators are essential in converting mechanical energy obtained from various sources such as steam turbines, water turbines, or internal combustion engines into electrical energy.
 
• The efficiency of an electric generator depends on several factors, including the strength of the magnetic field, the speed of rotation, and the design of the conductor coils.
 
• Modern electric generators are used in a wide range of applications, from small portable generators to large power plant generators.
